_comment: Guided tour of the model manager. Steps point at real controls. 'name' is the emtk control (table, action or attr); 'key' / 'action' with the toolbar glyph label keep the legacy Qt tool's spotlight working.

steps.title: Every model, and who offers it
steps.text: One row per registered fitting model. Click a header to sort, type in the filter box above the rows to keep rows containing the text, and read the Experiment column: the same model name can appear under more than one experiment.

steps.title: Pick one
steps.text: Click a row in the table. The pane on the right shows what the model computes, the class that implements it, and how its parameter panel is described.

await.hint: Click any row in the table.

steps.title: How the parameter panel is built
steps.text: Spec and Parameter UI together say whether a model's parameter panel comes from a declarative view spec — the direction the codebase is moving — or from Qt code the model still carries. A row reading missing file declares a spec that is not on disk, which is a real defect worth reporting.

steps.title: Switching a model off
steps.text: Disabled takes the selected model out of the drop-down without removing it. Watch the Shared column first: disabling matches on the name, so a name used by several experiments disables all of them at once. Show disabled models under the table hides or shows the switched-off rows.

steps.title: Entries that do nothing
steps.text: A disabled entry naming a model that no longer exists just sits there. The status line under the table counts them, and Drop stale clears them out after asking.

steps.title: Nothing is saved until you say so
steps.text: Save writes to your settings file; Revert throws the changes away after asking. The status line says unsaved changes until you save. The drop-down picks up a save the next time you select a dataset.
